title: Cohomology of schemes
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: The Leray–Hirsch map as a map of δ-functors, and dévissage from representable functors
modules.note:
A family θ of classes θ_i in Ext^{d_i}(Φ G, F), for an exact functor Φ, defines the Leray–Hirsch map
w ↦ Σ Φ(w_i) · θ_i. The file shows that its bijectivity at S can be proved by dévissage in S.

* `New.Variety.lerayHirsch`, `New.Variety.IsLerayHirschBasis`: the map, from finitely supported
  families in Ext(S, G) to Ext(Φ S, F), and its bijectivity.
* `New.Variety.isLerayHirschBasis_iff_allBijective_truncMap`: it is bijective iff its truncations to
  total degree below n all are.
* `New.Variety.Devissage.allBijective_of_allBijective_sigma_reprBy`: from disjoint unions of
  representable functors to all functors.
* `New.Variety.isLerayHirschBasis_of_reprBy`: from representable functors to all functors, for
  finitely many classes and Φ the restriction along a functor.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.H`: The group Ext^n(N,F) in the category of functors from C to abelian groups;
  `TotalH N F` is their direct sum over n, `x.toTotalH` is x placed in its degree, and
  `mapThenComp Φ t x` is the Yoneda product t ∘ Φ(x).
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to ℤ[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A).
* `New.Variety.Devissage`: The five and four lemmas for a family of maps f_{N,n} : A N n → B N n,
  indexed by functors N : D → Ab and degrees n, as for a map of contravariant δ-functors.
modules.literature:
Known result: Leray–Hirsch theorem that a local basis of cohomology classes is a global basis. The
theorem is stated abstractly for Ext groups of functors and finitely many classes. It says that if
the Leray–Hirsch map is bijective on ℤ[h_c] for every representable functor h_c, then it is
bijective on every functor. Source: Leray, Hirsch; Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, Thm 4D.1; SGA 5 VII
(projective bundle formula).

modules.title: Tensoring degree-two classes; cohomology theories with ℓ-torsion coefficients
modules.note:
The file works in categories of functors to abelian groups. First, a class in `Ext² (N, K)` between
functors with flat values is restricted along any functor and tensored with any abelian-group-valued
functor, compatibly (`New.Variety.exists_isTensorClass`). Then the cohomology of a space over `X` is
computed on the category of elements of `X`. Last, the file treats cohomology theories with
`ℓ`-torsion coefficients on categories over the test rings, families of ideals, and the theory of
locally constant functions.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsTensorClass`, `New.Variety.exists_isTensorClass`: a family of classes that extends
  `S ⊗ ξ` from functors `S` with flat values to all functors, and its existence.
* `New.Variety.hasUniversalPoints_elements`,
  `New.Variety.isBijective_relFreeAb_tautologicalSection`, `New.Variety.sliceEquiv`: cohomology of a
  space over `X` is computed on the category of elements of `X` (`New.Variety.elementsProj`).
* `New.Variety.InvertsPrime`, `New.Variety.TestOver`: a local absolutely integrally closed ring `A`
  in which `ℓ` is invertible, and the category of test rings over `A`.
* `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff`, `New.Variety.Theory`: coefficients with Zariski descent, and theories,
  where classes also extend from closed loci. `New.Variety.Theory.locallyConstant` is the theory of
  locally constant functions.
* `New.Variety.IdealFamily`, `New.Variety.Theory.onZeros`: a compatible family of ideals, and the
  coefficient that sees only the locus where it is zero.
* `New.Variety.IdealFamily.isCohomEquiv_constToZeros`,
  `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.pullbackAlong_oneLocConst_surjective`: the map from `ℤ/ℓ` relative to
  the locus where the ideal is the unit ideal to the locally constant functions on the zero locus is
  an equivalence for coefficients with Zariski descent, provided the locally constant functions
  along `g` underlie a theory `Θ`; hence every class on the constant functor `ℤ` with coefficients
  in a `TorsionCoeff g` (killed by `ℓ`, with Zariski descent) comes from one on the locally constant
  functions to `ℤ/ℓ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.HasFlatValues F`: every value of `F` is a flat `ℤ`-module.
* `New.Variety.restrictAlong φ`, `New.Variety.freeAb`: the functor `N ↦ N ∘ φ`, and the functor
  sending a set-valued functor `Y` to `ℤ[Y]`, the free abelian group on `Y(A)` at each `A`.
* `New.Variety.relFreeAb U`, `New.Variety.abCoker α`: the functor `ℤ[V]/ℤ[U]` for `U ⊆ V`, whose Ext
  groups are the relative cohomology of `(V, U)`; the cokernel of `α`, formed objectwise.
* `New.Variety.IsTest`: a test ring A is reduced and absolutely integrally closed, and any a, b ∈ A
  admit an idempotent e with a ∣ eb and b ∣ (1 − e)a.
* `New.Variety.Comparison`: a functor φ : C' → C with a map F∘φ → F'; it `IsBijective` along α :
  N' → N∘φ if Ext^n(N, F) → Ext^n(N', F') is bijective for all n. `HasUniversalPoints u`, a
  sufficient condition: the fibres of u over points are representable, with the same coefficients.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomDense`, `New.Variety.HasZariskiDescent`: `U ⊆ Y` is dense for `F` if, for
  every point `h_A → Y`, the inclusion of the preimage of `U` induces bijections on Ext with
  coefficients `F`; `F` has Zariski descent if every `U` that contains `Y` near each maximal ideal
  (`New.Variety.IsZariskiLocallyTop`) is dense for `F`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Cup product with a degree-two class and closed supports, for mod-ℓ cohomology as Ext.
Only the formal set-up is given, for Ext on test rings. It consists of ℓ-torsion coefficient
theories with closed supports cut out by families of ideals, and a degree-two class between flat
functors tensored with every functor. No Chern class, Künneth formula, Gysin map or Poincaré duality
is stated here. Source: for the setting, Milne, Étale Cohomology, Ch. VI.

See also `Lib.Cohomology.Etale.FilteredLimits` and `Lib.PadicComparison.Duality.GoodPairs`.

modules.title: Charted varieties, and smooth base change from a valuation ring to its fraction field
modules.note:
From local charts to whole varieties, for cohomology computed on test rings.

* `New.Variety.algToBaseChange`, `New.Variety.isBijective_algToBaseChange`: the cohomology of the
  base change `Y_A` on all test rings agrees with that of `Y` on tests over `A`
  (`New.Variety.TestOver`).
* `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.mem_of_isClosedClass_of_isCharting`: a class of functors governed by
  `New.Variety.ComparedTheory.IsFiniteLerayHirsch` that contains the point contains every functor
  charted by pieces étale over tori (`New.Variety.IsCharting`).
* `New.Variety.isTestCohomEquiv_baseChangeTransition`: let `A` be a valuation ring of an algebraic
  closure `Ω` of `ℚ`, of residue characteristic `p ≠ ℓ`, and let `Y` be charted; then the mod `ℓ`
  cohomology of `Y_A` and of `Y_Ω` agree.

`D.IsFiniteLerayHirsch N` says that the cohomology of `N` with locally constant `ZMod ℓ`
coefficients is finite and computes that of the theory `D`. The functor
`relFreeAb (offClosedFibre X)` is `ℤ[X] / ℤ[U]`, where `U` consists of the points over the tests in
which the maximal ideal of `A` generates the unit ideal.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to Z[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A).
* `New.Variety.IsClosedClass`: A closed class P of functors D → Ab: (a) P contains every zero
  functor N (written `𝟙 N = 0`); (b) for a short exact sequence 0 → X₁ → X₂ → X₃ → 0 with X₁ in P,
  the middle term X₂ is in P exactly when the quotient X₃ is.
* `New.Variety.geomPoints`: The functor of points of the base change `X ×_R Ω` of a scheme `X` over
  `R`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Smooth base change, with restriction to the generic fibre bijective on cohomology.
Here it is proved for schemes that are covered by finitely many pieces étale over tori and are not
assumed proper. The base is the valuation ring of a place above p of an algebraic closure of Q, the
coefficients are the constant F_ℓ with ℓ invertible, and the result is deduced from proper base
change and duality on products of projective lines. Source: Artin, SGA 4 Exp. XV 2.1, XVI 1.2
(1973); Stacks Project Tag 0EYQ; for the route through the class of the diagonal, Zavyalov, Poincaré
duality in abstract 6-functor formalisms (arXiv 2301.03821) and Li-Reinecke-Zavyalov (arXiv
2410.08200).

modules.title: Woods Hole (half of Atiyah–Bott): maps killed under λ_h on Hodge classes are h-null. Its head has an overview of the theory.
modules.note:
The main theorem, `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.woods_hole`: if a combination `∑ b_i u_i` of maps
`W → Y` kills all Hodge classes of `Y` under the Hodge–Tate map `λ_h` (`New.Variety.hodgeTateMap`),
then for every `c : W → Y` the local terms of weight `h` at the coincidences of `c` and the `u_i`
add up to zero (`New.Variety.IsNullFamily`). The proof pulls back the diagonal class of
`New.Variety.exists_diagonal_local_terms`, writes it as a sum of cross products
(`New.Variety.kunneth`) and takes the coefficient of `t ^ h` in the scaling parameter `t`: a linear
form does this (`Polynomial.exists_dual_eval_mul_eq_coeff_mul`), the pull-back of a cross product is
`New.Variety.map_scaledGraph_baseChange_cross`, and
`New.Variety.sum_mul_hodgeTateMap_scaledGraph_eq_zero` is the vanishing of the weighted sum.
`New.Variety.HodgeH` is Hodge cohomology, `New.Variety.algPoints` the functor of points, and
`New.Variety.HasAtlas` a finite cover by charts with `d` étale coordinates.

## Overview of this theory

Throughout, `ℓ` is a fixed prime. Cohomology of a functor `X` to sets, with coefficients in a
functor `F` to abelian groups, is `Extⁿ(ℤ[X], F)`. Here `ℤ[X]` is the free abelian group functor on
`X`, and the Ext is taken in functors on test objects: rings, or pairs of a ring and a module.

On absolutely integrally closed rings `A` (every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root),
locally constant functions on `Spec A` give `𝔽_ℓ`-cohomology. Their Witt vectors give
`ℤ_ℓ`-cohomology. `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom` is `X ↦ ℚ_ℓ ⊗ Hⁿ(X ×_R Ω, ℤ_ℓ)`, for `X` over a ring
`R` and an `R`-algebra `Ω`. Test objects may also be pairs `(B, M)` of a `k`-algebra `B` and a
`B`-module `M`. On these, `New.Variety.HodgeH` of a functor `N` in degree `q` is `Ext^q` from
`(B, M) ↦ N(B ⊕ M)` to `(B, M) ↦ ⋀_B M`.

* `New.Variety.IsProperOver.proper_base_change`: let `A` be an absolutely integrally closed local
  domain that is a valuation ring, with `ℓ` a unit in `A`. Let `Y` be proper over `Spec A`. Then
  restriction from `Y` to its closed fibre is bijective on `𝔽_ℓ`-cohomology in every degree.
* `New.Variety.isTestCohomEquiv_baseChangeTransition`: let `A` be a valuation ring of an algebraic
  closure `ℚ̄` of `ℚ`, with a prime `p` in its maximal ideal and `ℓ` a unit. Let `A` be an algebra
  over a ring `R`, and let `Y` over `R` be built from charts étale over tori
  (`New.Variety.IsCharted`). Then pull-back `Hⁿ(Y_A, 𝔽_ℓ) → Hⁿ(Y_ℚ̄, 𝔽_ℓ)` is bijective for all `n`.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.woods_hole`: let `R ⊆ E → k ⊆ ℚ̄_p`, with `E` a field of characteristic
  0 and `k` algebraically closed. Let `Y` be proper and `W` projective over `R`. Let `Y` over `E`
  and `W` over `k` have atlases of dimension `d`. Let `uᵢ : W ⟶ Y` be maps, and let `bᵢ ∈ k` be
  almost all zero. Let `λ_h` be the Hodge–Tate map `New.Variety.hodgeTateMap h`. Assume that
  `h > d`, or that `∑ bᵢ λ_h(uᵢ^* x) = 0`, read over `k`, for all `x` of degree at most `d` in
  `HodgeH` of `Y` over `E`. Then `New.Variety.IsNullFamily` holds: for `c : W ⟶ Y`, if each
  coincidence `c y = uᵢ y`, `y ∈ W(k)`, has a tangent polynomial `P` with `P(1) ≠ 0`, the terms
  `bᵢ · (coefficient of degree h of P) / P(1)` add up to zero.

These replace proper base change (SGA 4, XII) and smooth base change (SGA 4), here with coefficients
`𝔽_ℓ` over such rings. They also replace half of the holomorphic Lefschetz (Woods Hole) formula of
Atiyah and Bott, for `h`-forms and correspondences. No comparison with étale or coherent cohomology
is stated.

Structure of the development. `Etale`: descent, Mayer–Vietoris, limits, `ℓ`-adic coefficients.
`ProperBaseChange`: cover `X` by points with values in valuation rings, and reduce to the valuation
rings of a single field. `LerayHirsch`, `TorsionTheories`, `ProjectiveLine`: `1` and the first Chern
class of `O(1)` form a basis of the cohomology of `ℙ¹`. With duality from `Lib.PadicComparison`,
`SmoothBaseChange` follows. `Hodge`: point classes, the Künneth formula, local terms of the
diagonal. `PointClass`: the Hodge–Tate map of `Lib.PadicComparison` keeps distinct point classes
independent, by reduction to `ℙᵈ` and `ℙ¹`.

## This file

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.HodgeH.baseChange`: Base change: for an E-algebra k, the additive map from the Hodge
  cohomology over E of N to that over k of N restricted to k-algebras.
modules.literature:
Known result: Half of the holomorphic Lefschetz (Woods Hole) formula for h-forms and
correspondences. No trace is computed here. The statement is that if a combination of pull-backs
kills the Hodge classes of degree at most the dimension d under the Hodge–Tate map λ_h, then the z^h
coefficients of the local terms det(1−zA)/det(1−A) at simple coincidences add up to zero. Source:
M. F. Atiyah, R. Bott, A Lefschetz fixed point formula for elliptic complexes II, Ann. of Math. 88
(1968) 451-491; G. Kondyrev, A. Prikhodko, Holomorphic Atiyah-Bott formula for correspondences,
Arnold Math. J. (2022); SGA5 III 6.12.

modules.title: Cohomology of functors as Ext: test rings, points, functoriality, coefficients
modules.group: Étale-type cohomology of functors of points
modules.note:
Fix a category `C` of test objects and a coefficient functor `F : C ⥤ Ab`. A space is a functor
`Y : C ⥤ Type 1`, and its cohomology is `New.Variety.H N F n = Extⁿ(N, F)` with `N = ℤ[Y]`, computed
in the category `New.Variety.AbFunctor C` of functors `C ⥤ Ab`. Here `H.map` is pull-back in `N` and
`H.push` is push-forward in `F`. In the main case `C` is the category of test rings, a scheme is
replaced by its functor of points, and `F` sends `A` to the locally constant functions `Spec A → Λ`
for an abelian group `Λ`. The file proves stability properties of test rings, formal functoriality
of `H` and the additive Yoneda lemma, and it fixes vocabulary for fixed point formulas and
congruence relations with Frobenius.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.H N F n = Extⁿ(N, F)` and `New.Variety.freeAb` (the functor `Y ↦ ℤ[Y]`), with
  pull-back `New.Variety.H.map` in `N` and push-forward `New.Variety.H.push` in `F`.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomEquiv F α`: `α` is bijective on all `Extⁿ(-, F)`.
  `New.Variety.IsCohomDense F U`: the subfunctor `U` gives such an equivalence over every point
  `New.Variety.pointMap y`.
* `New.Variety.IsTest`, `New.Variety.TestRing`: test rings and their category. A test ring is
  reduced and absolutely integrally closed, and divisibility in it is total after a partition by an
  idempotent.
* `New.Variety.locConstCoeff`, `New.Variety.TestCohomology.map`: the coefficients A ↦ {locally
  constant Spec A → Λ} on test rings, and pull-back on cohomology.
* `New.Variety.IsTest.pi`, `New.Variety.IsTest.localization`, `New.Variety.IsTest.quotient`:
  products, localisations and quotients by radical ideals of test rings are test rings.
* `New.Variety.H.dimension_shift_induction`: induction on classes by dimension shifting. Identities
  between maps of `Ext` groups are checked in degree zero and on connecting maps.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed`: A is absolutely integrally closed: every monic polynomial
  over A of positive degree has a root in A.

modules.title: Criteria for comparison maps of Ext cohomology of functors of points to be bijective
modules.group: Étale-type cohomology of functors of points
modules.note:
For a set-valued functor of points `Y` on a category `C` with coefficients `F`, cohomology is
`Hⁿ(Y, F) = New.Variety.H (freeAb.obj Y) F n`, an `Ext` group in functors to abelian groups, where
`ℤ[Y]` is the free abelian functor on `Y`; `reprBy A` is the functor `B ↦ (A ⟶ B)` (lifted), and a
point `y` of `Y A` gives `pointMap y : reprBy A ⟶ Y`, `f ↦ Y.map f y`. A comparison `c = (φ, β)`
with `φ : C' ⥤ C` and `β : φ ⋙ F ⟶ F'`, together with a map `u : Y' ⟶ φ ⋙ Y`, gives maps
`c.pull (freeAbMap u) n : Hⁿ(Y, F) → Hⁿ(Y', F')`. The file gives criteria for these maps to be
bijective. The tools are dévissage and Čech descent along covers, and pointwise descriptions of
bijections and pull-back squares. The file also builds cocycle classes from witnesses of a relation
`R ⊆ V × L`, relative to a subfunctor `U ⊆ V`, by a Čech-type complex.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.witnessed.universalClass`, `New.Variety.witnessed.cocycleClass`: splicing the short
  exact sequences into which the complex of points with witnesses splits gives a universal class;
  its push-forward along a cocycle with values in `F` is a class in `Extⁿ(ℤ[V]/ℤ[U], F)`.
* `New.Variety.cech_descent_step`, `New.Variety.Devissage.allBijective_freeAb_range_of_cech`: Čech
  descent of bijectivity from `E` and its fibre powers `New.Variety.cech p m` to the image of
  `p : E ⟶ Y`.
* `New.Variety.IsCover`: `p` is a cover for `F`, that is, the inclusion of its image induces
  bijections on all `Extⁿ(ℤ[-], F)`; pointwise surjections are covers
  (`New.Variety.IsPointwiseSurjective.isCover`).
* `New.Variety.Comparison.IsBijective`: for a natural map `α : N' ⟶ c.functor ⋙ N`, the maps
  `c.pull α n : Extⁿ(N, F) → Extⁿ(N', F')` are bijective in all degrees; for `α = freeAbMap u` these
  are the maps `Hⁿ(Y, F) → Hⁿ(Y', F')`.
* `New.Variety.Comparison.isBijective_of_fibres`: it is enough to test on the fibres over the points
  of `Y`; the proof is Čech descent (`New.Variety.Comparison.bijectiveUpTo_of_cech_pred`), one
  condition of `New.Variety.BijectiveUpTo` at a time.
* `New.Variety.Comparison.HasUniversalPoints.isBijective`: representable fibres with equal
  coefficients (`New.Variety.Comparison.IsUnivPoint`) suffice;
  `New.Variety.Comparison.isBijective_of_adj` is the case of an adjunction.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.H`: The group Ext^n(N,F) in the category of functors from C to abelian groups;
  `H.map F α n` is the pull-back along α: N' → N and `H.push N β n` the push-forward along β:
  F → F'.
* `New.Variety.Comparison`: A comparison from F on C to F' on C' is a functor φ: C' → C with a map
  β: F∘φ → F'. For α: N' → N∘φ, `Comparison.pull` is the map Ext^n(N,F) → Ext^n(N',F') that
  restricts along φ, pushes by β and pulls by α.
* `New.Variety.BijectiveUpTo`: For maps f_n: A_n → B_n, the first r of the conditions: f₀ injective,
  f₀ surjective, f₁ injective, f₁ surjective, and so on.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomEquiv`: α: N' → N is an equivalence for F: the pull-back
  Ext^n(N,F) → Ext^n(N',F) is bijective for every n.
* `New.Variety.freeAbMap`: For u: Y' → Y∘φ, the induced map of free abelian group functors
  Z[Y'] → Z[Y]∘φ.

modules.title: Dense subfunctors, Mayer–Vietoris and partitions along idempotents
modules.group: Étale-type cohomology of functors of points
modules.note:
This file studies the cohomology Hⁿ(Y) = Extⁿ(ℤ[Y], F) of a set-valued functor Y on a category C
with coefficients in a functor F : C → Ab, where ℤ[Y] = `New.Variety.freeAb` Y. A map is an
equivalence for F (`New.Variety.IsCohomEquiv`) if it induces bijections on all Extⁿ(-, F). A
subfunctor U of Y is dense (`New.Variety.IsCohomDense`) if, over every point h_A → Y with h_A =
Hom(A,−), the inclusion of the preimage of U is an equivalence. The Mayer–Vietoris sequence, the
calculus of dense subfunctors and closed classes of functors are used to cut functors into pieces.
When ι attaches commutative rings to objects and `New.Variety.HasPartitions ι F` holds, partitions
along idempotents are dense. Locally constant coefficients on test rings satisfy
`New.Variety.HasPartitions`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.mayer_vietoris_shortExact`: 0 → ℤ[U ∩ V] → ℤ[U] ⊕ ℤ[V] → ℤ[U ∪ V] → 0 is short exact.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomDense.isCohomEquiv`: the inclusion of a dense subfunctor is an equivalence.
* `New.Variety.IsClosedClass.freeAb_iSup`: if a closed class contains ℤ[V] for all V in a set of
  subfunctors closed under intersection, it contains ℤ[-] of their finite unions (Mayer–Vietoris).
* `New.Variety.HasPartitions.isCohomDense_partition`: for an idempotent `e`, the maps that kill `e`
  or `1 - e` are dense.
* `New.Variety.HasPartitions.hasZariskiDescent`: Zariski descent for rings `κ` that receive an
  injective map from `ι`, when any two elements of `κ` are comparable for divisibility after a cut
  along an idempotent of `ι`.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomDense.isCohomEquiv_of_fromPreimage`: a map is an equivalence if it is one over
  a dense subfunctor.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to ℤ[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A).
* `New.Variety.IsClosedClass`: a class of functors C → Ab that contains every zero functor and, for
  a short exact sequence whose first term lies in it, contains the middle term exactly when it
  contains the last.
* `New.Variety.HasPartitions`: Each idempotent e ≠ 1 of ι(A) has a `New.Variety.IsQuotientByElem`
  A → B, and ι(A) ≅ ι(B₁) × ι(B₂) via maps A → B₁, B₂ implies F(A) ≅ F(B₁) × F(B₂).

modules.title: Continuity of cohomology along filtered limits, via test rings and relatively affine maps
modules.group: Étale-type cohomology of functors of points
modules.note:
The cohomology of a set-valued functor `Y` on rings is Hⁿ(Y) = Extⁿ(ℤ[Y], F). Here ℤ[Y] is the free
abelian group functor, and h_A = Hom(A, −) is the functor represented by `A`. The question is when
Hⁿ turns a cofiltered limit of functors into a filtered colimit of groups. Cohomology is computed on
test rings, with coefficients the locally constant functions to an abelian group Λ. Test rings have
no higher cohomology, and their cohomology commutes with filtered colimits. Relatively affine maps
are maps whose pull-backs to representable functors are representable.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.ContinuousUpTo`: for a cone `c` over a cofiltered diagram `D` of set-valued functors,
  the maps colim_j Hⁿ(D j) → Hⁿ(c.pt) satisfy the first `r` conditions of
  `New.Variety.BijectiveUpTo`.
* `New.Variety.ContinuousUpTo.of_cech`: the property descends along covers, by
  `New.Variety.cech_descent_step`.
* `New.Variety.continuousUpTo_locConstCoeff`: the cohomology of test rings, with locally constant
  coefficients, commutes with filtered colimits.
* `New.Variety.Envelope.exists_natTrans_isTest_and_factors`: a functorial map θ : A → E(A) to a test
  ring through which, for A in a given family, every map to a test ring factors.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomContinuous`: continuity over X, for coefficients Λ. On a filtered inverse
  system of functors affine over X, the cohomology of the limit is the colimit of the cohomologies.
  `New.Variety.IsCohomContinuous.of_isRelAffine` passes it to functors affine over X.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomContinuous.of_hasCohomDenseImage`: continuity holds over Y if a representable
  functor h_T maps to Y by a map that is affine and has dense image.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsTest`: A is a test ring: reduced, absolutely integrally closed, and any a, b admit
  an idempotent e with a ∣ eb and b ∣ (1 − e)a. `New.Variety.TestRing` is their category.
* `New.Variety.IsCover`: p: E → Y is a cover for F: the inclusion of the image of p in Y induces
  bijections on Ext^n(Z[−],F) for all n.
* `New.Variety.locConstCoeff`: For an abelian group Λ, the coefficient functor on test rings sending
  A to the group of locally constant functions Spec A → Λ.
* `New.Variety.BijectiveUpTo`: for maps f_n : A_n → B_n, the first r of the conditions f₀
  injective, f₀ surjective, f₁ injective, f₁ surjective, and so on.
modules.literature:
Known result: Descent of torsion étale cohomology along v-covers, with excision, transfer and
limits. Here cohomology is defined as Ext of presheaves on test rings. The local rings of a test
ring are valuation rings of algebraically closed fields. Descent, excision, transfer and limits are
proved from this definition, while equality with étale cohomology is neither proved nor used.
Source: Scholze, Berkovich Motives, arXiv 2412.03382 (2024), Thm 4.1 and Lemmas 4.7, 4.8 (descent
and limits from finitary functors on test rings); Bhatt, Mathew, The arc-topology, Duke Math. J. 170
(2021), Prop 5.2, Thm 5.4; Stacks project, Tag 09YQ; Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds,
7.15-7.16.

See also `Lib.Cohomology.ProperBaseChange.Theorem`.

modules.title: Relative chains ℤ[V]/ℤ[U]: local isomorphisms, transfer, excision and gluing
modules.group: Étale-type cohomology of functors of points
modules.note:
This file provides tools for computing the groups Ext^n(N, F) (`New.Variety.H`) of functors from a
category C to abelian groups. For a subfunctor U of a set-valued functor V,
`New.Variety.relFreeAb U` is the quotient ℤ[V]/ℤ[U] of free abelian groups (`New.Variety.freeAb`).
Its Ext^n into F is the relative cohomology H^n(V, U). A map is an equivalence for F
(`New.Variety.IsCohomEquiv`) if it is bijective on all Ext^n(·, F). A subfunctor U of Y is dense
(`New.Variety.IsCohomDense`) if over every point h_A → Y its preimage gives an equivalence; with
these notions the file proves vanishing for locally zero functors, transfer, excision and gluing of
relative classes over finite covers.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.cohomology_eq_zero_of_locallyZero`, `New.Variety.isCohomEquiv_of_locallyZero`: a
  functor whose sections all die on dense sieves has no cohomology, so a map with such a kernel and
  cokernel is an equivalence.
* `New.Variety.exists_transfer_map`: the transfer attached to finitely many locally permuted maps
  (`New.Variety.permutedPairs`: the pairs on which they are permuted).
* `New.Variety.relFreeAb.shortExact_triple`, `New.Variety.relFreeAb.isCohomEquiv_of_le`,
  `New.Variety.relFreeAb.excision`: the exact sequence of a monomorphism, invariance under enlarging
  U′ to U when U′ is dense in U, and excision.
* `New.Variety.relFreeAb.exists_glued_class`: in the lowest degree where it may be nonzero, relative
  cohomology glues over a finite cover (a Mayer–Vietoris induction).
* `New.Variety.relFreeAb.prod`: the map of pairs that gives exterior products of relative classes.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.isCohomEquiv_iff_subsingleton`, `New.Variety.isCohomEquiv_quotient_of_acyclic`: for
  0 → X₁ → X₂ → X₃ → 0 short exact, X₁ → X₂ is an equivalence for F exactly when all Ext^n(X₃, F)
  vanish, and X₂ → X₃ is one when all Ext^n(X₁, F) vanish.
* `New.Variety.pointMap`: The map h_A → Y from h_A = Hom(A,−) corresponding to a point y of Y(A) by
  the Yoneda lemma.

modules.title: ℓ-adic cohomology with its Galois action; finiteness and bijectivity from coefficients mod ℓ
modules.group: Étale-type cohomology of functors of points
modules.note:
`ℓ`-adic cohomology is defined as `Ext` on test rings, with coefficients in the Witt vectors of the
locally constant `𝔽_ℓ`-valued functions on the spectrum.

* `New.Variety.ellAdicCoeff`: the coefficient `ℤ_ℓ`; `New.Variety.ellAdicPull`: pull-back on
  cohomology, over `ℚ_ℓ`.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom`, `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.galoisAction`: cohomology of the base change
  to `Ω`, and the action of `Γ`.
* `New.Variety.exists_ellAdicCoeff_modShortExact_pow`,
  `New.Variety.exists_ellAdicCoeff_modShortExact`: reduction modulo `ℓ ^ k` and `ℓ`; completeness.
* `New.Variety.finite_H_ellAdicCoeff`, `New.Variety.IsCohomEquiv.bijective_ellAdicPull`: finiteness
  and bijectivity lift from `𝔽_ℓ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.ModShortExact`: `ModShortExact a q` says that `0 → Φ → Φ → G → 0`, formed by
  multiplication by `a` and by `q`, is short exact.
* `New.Variety.TestRing`: The category of test rings (`New.Variety.IsTest`), as a full subcategory
  of commutative rings; `New.Variety.testIncl` is its inclusion functor.

modules.title: Local-to-global principle, density criteria and proper functors for cohomology on test rings
modules.group: Étale-type cohomology of functors of points
modules.note:
This file studies the cohomology `Hⁿ(Y) = Extⁿ(ℤ[Y], F)` of set-valued functors `Y` on rings,
computed on test rings, with `F = New.Variety.locConstCoeff Λ` the locally constant `Λ`-valued
functions. Two criteria for density, for affine maps and for finitely many affine subfunctors, are
tested on points in valuation rings of algebraically closed fields.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsTestCohomEquiv.of_connected`: the local-to-global principle. A map
  `u : X ⟶ Y` that induces isomorphisms on cohomology (`New.Variety.IsTestCohomEquiv`) over every
  connected piece of `Y` induces them over `Y`. This needs `X` and `Y` cohomologically continuous
  (`New.Variety.IsCohomContinuous`). The pieces are loci `U a` of a zero-locus family `U` with
  `U (span {e}) ⊔ U (span {1 - e})` dense for every idempotent `e`.
* `New.Variety.IsRelAffine.hasCohomDenseImage_of_lifts`: an affine map that is onto on such points
  has dense image.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomDense.of_affine_cover`: `U` is dense if each such point lies in one of
  finitely many affine subfunctors whose points in test rings belong to `U`.
* `New.Variety.IsProperOver.hasCohomDenseImage_of_surjective`: a map of proper functors, onto on
  geometric points, has dense image (`New.Variety.IsCohomDense`) for locally constant coefficients
  `New.Variety.locConstCoeff Λ`.
* A density criterion for finitely many maps `P i : Y ⟶ Z` into a proper functor:
  `New.Variety.IsProperOver.isCohomDense_of_coincidences`. It is
  `New.Variety.IsCohomDense.of_affine_cover` for the closed loci on which prescribed pairs of the
  maps agree.
* `New.Variety.ellAdicCohom.transfer`: let `c : W ⟶ Y` be a Galois covering of proper schemes with
  finite group `Δ`. Then the `ℓ`-adic cohomology of `Y` embeds in that of `W` and reaches all
  `Δ`-invariant classes.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsRelAffine`: The property of a map X → Y of set-valued functors on rings that its
  pull-back along every point h_A → Y is representable, of the form h_B → h_A.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomDense`: The subfunctor U of Y is dense for F: for every point h_A → Y, the
  inclusion of the preimage of U in h_A is an equivalence for F.
* `New.Variety.reprBy`: The functor h_A = Hom(A,−) represented by the object A.
* `New.Variety.IsTest`: a test ring A is reduced and absolutely integrally closed, and any a, b ∈ A
  admit an idempotent e with a ∣ eb and b ∣ (1 − e)a.
* `New.Variety.IsProperOver`: The functor Z on rings is proper over D: its diagonal is closed, and
  it satisfies a valuative criterion for valuation rings of algebraically closed fields.
* `New.Variety.locConstCoeff`: For an abelian group Λ, the coefficient functor on test rings sending
  A to the group of locally constant functions Spec A → Λ.

modules.title: Pointwise tensor product of functors, total Ext with Yoneda composition, external products
modules.group: Hodge cohomology, symbols and the fixed point formula
modules.note:
Products in the cohomology `New.Variety.H N F n = Ext^n(N, F)` of functors from `C` to abelian
groups (`New.Variety.AbFunctor C`).

* `New.Variety.abTensor`, `New.Variety.HasFlatValues`: the pointwise tensor product, exact for flat
  values.
* `New.Variety.TotalH`: the direct sum of all `Ext^n(N, F)`, with the Yoneda product
  `New.Variety.TotalH.comp` and the action `New.Variety.TotalH.map` of exact functors
  (`IsExactFunctor`: sending exact sequences to exact sequences). Pull-back and push-forward become
  products with classes of degree zero, so degrees need no tracking.
* `New.Variety.TotalH.exact_triangle`: the long exact sequence, as an exact triangle.
* `New.Variety.cup`: the external product, natural in the spaces (`New.Variety.cup_map`) and in the
  site (`New.Variety.Comparison.pull_cup`).

`comp x y` is written in diagram order: `x` in `TotalH M N`, `y` in `TotalH N F`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.H.map`, `New.Variety.H.push`: the maps Ext^n(N,F) → Ext^n(N',F) and
  Ext^n(N,F) → Ext^n(N,F') given by α: N' → N and β: F → F'.
* `New.Variety.Comparison`: a comparison from F on C to F' on C' is a functor φ: C' → C with a
  natural transformation β: F∘φ → F' (the field `coeffHom`).
* `New.Variety.Comparison.pull`: for a comparison (φ,β) and α: N' → N∘φ, the homomorphism
  Ext^n(N,F) → Ext^n(N',F') obtained by restricting along φ, pushing by β and pulling by α.
* `New.Variety.restrictAlong`: for a functor φ: C' → C and a category D, the functor N ↦ N∘φ from
  functors C → D to functors C' → D.

modules.title: Hodge cohomology on algebras with free modules; universal points of charts
modules.group: Hodge cohomology, symbols and the fixed point formula
modules.note:
This file makes the pairs (A, M) of a k-algebra A and a free module M = A^ι
(`New.Variety.HodgeTest`) into a category and defines Hodge cohomology on it. A morphism is a
k-algebra map a together with an a-semilinear map of the modules. A functor of points N on
k-algebras is evaluated on the square-zero extension A ⊕ M, which sees tangent vectors.

* `New.Variety.HodgeTest.sqZeroExt`, `New.Variety.exteriorAlg`: the functors (A, M) ↦ A ⊕ M
  and (A, M) ↦ ⋀_A M.
* `New.Variety.HodgeH`: Hodge cohomology, Ext^q from N(A ⊕ M) to ⋀_A M in functors on pairs, with
  pull-back `New.Variety.HodgeH.map`, scaling `New.Variety.HodgeH.scale` and base change
  `New.Variety.HodgeH.baseChange`.
* `New.Variety.HodgeTest.existsUnique_lift_away`: maps out of (A[1/g], A[1/g]^ι) are the maps
  out of (A, A^ι) that invert g.
* `New.Variety.EtaleChart.univPoint`, `New.Variety.EtaleChart.exists_univPoint`: for a chart with
  ring R and d étale coordinates, the point through which the pair (R, R^d) represents
  (A, M) ↦ Hom(R, A ⊕ M).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.HodgeTest`: a pair (A, M) as above, given by A and a finite ordered index set ι.
* `New.Variety.moduleCoeff`: a functor F from C to k-modules, regarded as a functor to abelian
  groups, so that it can serve as the coefficients of cohomology.
* `New.Variety.Comparison`: a functor φ : C' ⥤ C with a map φ ⋙ F ⟶ F' of coefficients; its `pull`
  along α : N' ⟶ φ ⋙ N maps Ext^n(N, F) to Ext^n(N', F').
* `New.Variety.EtaleChart`: a chart of X: a k-algebra R with finitely many étale coordinates and a
  point y in X(R) that embeds Spec R as an open subfunctor.
* `New.Variety.pointMap`: the map h_A → Y corresponding to a point y of Y(A) by the Yoneda lemma;
  here h_A = `New.Variety.reprBy A` is the functor of maps out of A.

modules.title: Vanishing of Hodge cohomology with supports below the depth, and Zariski descent
modules.group: Hodge cohomology, symbols and the fixed point formula
modules.note:
* `New.Variety.depth_vanishing`: the abstract induction on a regular sequence.
* `New.Variety.DepthVanishing.subsingleton_of_isWeaklyRegular`: for a pair `c = (A, M)`, the
  cohomology of `h_c` relative to the locus `New.Variety.someUnitLocus f` where some `f i` is a unit
  vanishes below the depth of the ideal `(f)`.
* `New.Variety.hodge_vanishing_along_diagonal`: on a chart with étale coordinates `x_1, …, x_{2d}`
  and the ideal of the `x_i - x_{d+i}` (the diagonal), it vanishes in degrees below `d`.
* `New.Variety.isCohomEquiv_someUnitLocus_of_span_eq_top`,
  `New.Variety.hasZariskiDescent_hodgeCoeff`: for the unit ideal it vanishes in all degrees, which
  gives Zariski descent for Hodge cohomology.

`New.Variety.H N F n` is `Ext^n(N, F)` in functors to abelian groups, `New.Variety.relFreeAb U` is
`ℤ[V] / ℤ[U]` for `U ⊆ V`, and `New.Variety.hodgeCoeff` is the coefficient functor `(A, M) ↦ ⋀_A M`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.HodgeTest`: a test for Hodge cohomology over k, namely a commutative k-algebra A and
  a finite index set ι, standing for the pair (A, M) with M = A^ι.
* `New.Variety.reprBy`: the functor h_A = Hom(A,−) represented by the object A.

modules.title: Grothendieck's symbol [dT/T], cut-out loci and Hodge classes of points
modules.group: Hodge cohomology, symbols and the fixed point formula
modules.note:
Let `k` be a field (of characteristic zero for `symbolClass_succ`). Spaces are functors `X` from
`k`-algebras to sets. `New.Variety.HodgeH (relFreeAb U) d` is the Hodge cohomology of `X` relative
to a subfunctor `U`, and `New.Variety.offPoints s` is the complement of a set `s` of `k`-points;
`ComesFromPoints s K x` says that `x ∈ X(K)` is the image of some `z ∈ s`. Grothendieck's symbol
`New.Variety.symbolClass` is a class in the Hodge cohomology of affine d-space relative to the
complement of the origin. `[dg / g]` denotes its pull-back along a tuple of functions `g`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus X P x f` says that the elements `f i` of `R` cut out the locus of
  `Spec R` where the point `x` of `X(R)` satisfies `P`.
* `New.Variety.symbolClass`: the class, given by the cocycle (v, l_1, …, l_d) ↦ det(l) · dT(v).
* `New.Variety.symbolClass_transformation`: the transformation law between the pull-backs along two
  tuples.
* `New.Variety.symbolClass_succ`: the class in degree d + 1 restricts to the product of the classes
  in degrees d and 1.
* `New.Variety.IsPointSum`: near each `z ∈ s`, a relative class is `n z • [dg / g]` for functions
  `g` that cut out `z`; `New.Variety.pointClass` is the image of a chosen class of multiplicity `1`.
* `New.Variety.IsPointSum.map_eq_smul_pointClass`, `New.Variety.IsPointSum.map_eq_sum_pointClass`:
  on a separated `X`, a class with support in a finite set `s` and multiplicities `n` maps to
  `∑ z ∈ s, n z • pointClass d z`. The proof is by excision for one point and by Mayer–Vietoris for
  several.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.unimodular`: The subfunctor of affine d-space of vectors whose entries generate the
  unit ideal.
* `New.Variety.pointMap`: The map Hom(A, −) → Y given by a point y of Y(A) (Yoneda).
* `New.Variety.IsSeparatedFunctor`: X is separated: for x, y in X(A) there is an ideal J of A such
  that φ: A → B makes x and y equal exactly when φ kills J.
* `New.Variety.HodgeTest`: a test for Hodge cohomology over k, namely a commutative k-algebra A and
  a finite index set ι, standing for the pair (A, M) with M = A^ι.
* `New.Variety.HodgeTest.sqZeroExt`: The functor sending a pair (A, M) to the square-zero extension
  A ⊕ M, as a k-algebra.
* `New.Variety.hodgeCoeff`: The functor (A, M) ↦ ⋀_A M to abelian groups, the coefficients.
* `New.Variety.EtaleChart`: A chart of X: a k-algebra R with finitely many étale coordinates and a
  point of X(R) that embeds Spec R as an open subfunctor (its image is `a.locus`).
* `New.Variety.HodgeH`: Hodge cohomology: for a functor N from k-algebras to abelian groups, Ext^q
  from (A, M) ↦ N(A ⊕ M) to (A, M) ↦ ⋀_A M, in functors on pairs.

modules.title: Künneth formula: Hodge classes on X × X are sums of external products
modules.group: Hodge cohomology, symbols and the fixed point formula
modules.note:
The Künneth formula for Hodge cohomology `New.Variety.HodgeH`, in the weak form that the fixed-point
formula needs: cross products span.

* `New.Variety.kunneth`: over a field of characteristic 0, if `X` has an atlas, every class on
  `X × X` is a sum of cross products of classes on `X`.

Hodge cohomology is an Ext group in functors on pairs `(A, M)`, where `M` is a finite free
`A`-module (`New.Variety.HodgeTest`). It is taken from `(A, M) ↦ ℤ[X(A ⊕ M)]` to the exterior
algebra `(A, M) ↦ ⋀ M` (`New.Variety.hodgeCoeff`).

The proof first treats a product of two represented functors through the Leray–Hirsch map. It then
passes to the general case by dévissage in each factor.

Notions from other files:
* `CategoryTheory.Functor.mulPairing`: For a functor Φ to k-algebras with underlying functor F to
  abelian groups, the pairing F ⊗ F → F given by multiplication.
* `New.Variety.exteriorAlg`: The functor sending a pair (A, M) to the exterior algebra ⋀_A M, as a
  k-algebra.
* `New.Variety.lerayHirsch`: For an exact functor Φ and classes θ_i in Ext^{d_i}(ΦG, F), the map
  w ↦ Σ θ_i∘Φ(w_i) from finitely supported families in total Ext(S, G) to total Ext(ΦS, F).
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to Z[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A).
* `New.Variety.abTensor`: The pointwise tensor product over ℤ of two functors from C to abelian
  groups, as a bifunctor.
* `New.Variety.H`, `New.Variety.TotalH`: The group Ext^n(N, F) in functors to abelian groups, and
  the direct sum of these groups over n.

modules.title: The Hodge class of the diagonal of a variety with an atlas, with its local description
modules.group: Hodge cohomology, symbols and the fixed point formula
modules.note:
The class of the diagonal in Hodge cohomology, for a functor of points `X` on `k`-algebras.

* `New.Variety.exists_diagonal_class`: if `k` has characteristic zero and `X` has an atlas of
  dimension `d`, there is a class `δ` of degree `d` on `X × X` relative to the complement of the
  diagonal that is, near the diagonal, the symbol `[df / f]` of the differences of chart
  coordinates. It is glued from such symbols.

`New.Variety.HasAtlas d X`: `X` is separated and its field points lie in finitely many affine charts
`New.Variety.EtaleChart d X` with `d` étale coordinates. `HodgeH (relFreeAb U) q` is Hodge
cohomology relative to the subfunctor `U`. `New.Variety.IsLocalSymbol ξ y P g m` says three things:
`g` cuts out `P` at the point `y`; `y` maps the part of `Spec R` off the preimage of `P` into `U`;
and `ξ` pulls back along `y` to `m • [dg / g]`. Here `[dg / g]` is the pull-back of
`New.Variety.symbolClass` along `g`. `P` is a predicate on points, not the subfunctor that `ξ` is
relative to; that subfunctor is the implicit `U`. For the diagonal class, `P` is the diagonal
`x.1 = x.2`, while `δ` is relative to its complement.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus`: The elements `f i` of `R` cut out the locus where the point `x` of
  `X(R)` satisfies `P`: a map `α : R ⟶ C` kills every `f i` exactly when the image of `x` in `X(C)`
  satisfies `P`.
* `New.Variety.IsOpenSubfunctor`: V is an open subfunctor of X: each x ∈ X(A) has an ideal I of A
  such that, for φ: A → B, φ(x) ∈ V(B) iff φ(I)B = B.
* `New.Variety.EtaleChart`: A chart of X: a k-algebra R with finitely many étale coordinates and a
  point y in X(R) that embeds Spec R as an open subfunctor, its `locus`.
* `New.Variety.offDiagonal`: The complement of the diagonal in X × X: pairs of points whose values
  in every field are distinct.
* `New.Variety.relFreeAb`: For a subfunctor U of a set-valued functor V, the functor to abelian
  groups ℤ[V]/ℤ[U].
* `New.Variety.HodgeH`: Hodge cohomology: for a functor N from k-algebras to abelian groups, Ext^q
  from (A, M) ↦ N(A ⊕ M) to (A, M) ↦ ⋀_A M, in functors on pairs.

modules.title: Reduced coincidences and the fixed point formula in Hodge cohomology
modules.group: Hodge cohomology, symbols and the fixed point formula
modules.note:
Let `W`, `X` be functors from `k`-algebras to sets (`New.Variety.CommAlg k ⥤ Type 1`), standing for
schemes, and let `u c : W ⟶ X` be two maps. A coincidence is a point `x` of `W` with `c x = u x`.
The file proves the fixed point formula in Hodge cohomology `Hdg^d(W)`, that is
`HodgeH (freeAb.obj W) d`, computed on square-zero extensions `A ⊕ M`: a pulled-back diagonal class
is a sum of point classes `New.Variety.pointClass d w` over the coincidences, weighted by Jacobian
determinants. If `k` is algebraically closed, `X` is separated, every `k[ε]`-valued coincidence is
constant and finitely many charts of `W` contain all field-valued coincidences, then the
coincidences form a finite set of rational points, which carry these local terms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.ConstIfCoincident`, `New.Variety.IsCoincidenceSet`: reduced coincidences, and a
  finite set of rational points that lists them all.
* `New.Variety.HasJacobianRatio`: the local term, the determinant of `(t du - dc) (du - dc)⁻¹`.
* `New.Variety.IsTangentPoly.hasJacobianRatio_eval_div`: a tangent polynomial `P` with `P 1 ≠ 0`
  gives this term as `P t / P 1`; by `New.Variety.IsTangentPoly.constIfCoincident` the coincidences
  at that point are then reduced.
* `New.Variety.scaledGraph`: the graph of `(u, c)` twisted by the scaling of `M` by `t` in the first
  factor.
* `New.Variety.exists_diagonal_local_terms`: the class `δ` of the diagonal, pulled back along this
  twisted graph, is `∑ n w • pointClass d w` over the coincidences `w` of `u` and `c`, where `n w`
  is the determinant of a matrix `N` with `t du - dc = N (du - dc)` at `w`
  (`New.Variety.HasJacobianRatio`).
* `New.Variety.IsPointSum.cup_pointClass`: the external product of the class of a point of `X` and
  the class of a point of a curve is the class of the product point.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.HodgeH`: Hodge cohomology: for a functor N from k-algebras to abelian groups, Ext^q
  from (A, M) ↦ N(A ⊕ M) to (A, M) ↦ ⋀_A M, in functors on pairs.
* `New.Variety.symbolClass`: The Grothendieck symbol [dT/T] in Hdg^d(𝔸^d, 𝔸^d ∖ 0); its pull-back
  along a tuple f of functions is the symbol [df/f].
* `New.Variety.IsPointSum`: A relative class has multiplicity n z at each z in s: on some chart
  containing z it restricts to n z times the symbol [dg / g] of functions g that cut out z.
* `New.Variety.IsTangentPoly`: at a point `y ∈ W(k)`, the tangent map `dc` on the tangent space of
  dimension `d` is injective, `du = dc ∘ B`, and `P t = P 0 * det (1 - t B)`.
* `New.Variety.HasAtlas`: X is separated and has finitely many charts, each with exactly d étale
  coordinates, that contain every field-valued point.
* `New.Variety.offPoints`: for a set s of k-points of X, the subfunctor of the points none of whose
  values in fields comes from s.
* `New.Variety.exteriorAlg`, `CategoryTheory.Functor.mulPairing`: the exterior algebra ⋀_A M of a
  pair (A, M), and the pairing given by its multiplication (the wedge product of coefficients in the
  cup product).
* `New.Variety.freeAb.prod`: for set-valued functors X, Y, the map ℤ[X × Y] → ℤ[X] ⊗ ℤ[Y], [(x,
  y)] ↦ [x] ⊗ [y].
modules.literature:
Known result: the fixed point formula in Hodge cohomology, with local terms computed by
Grothendieck symbols. Here the setting is characteristic 0 and smooth separated varieties with a
finite atlas, with cohomology taken as Ext of functors. The class of the diagonal and Künneth
surjectivity for X×X are not proved here; they come from `exists_diagonal_class` and `kunneth` in
other files. Here the point classes are multiplied for a product with a curve, and the pull-back of
the diagonal class along reduced coincidences is given as a weighted sum of point classes. Source:
Stacks Project, tags 0BEC (Künneth) and 0G82 (Gysin maps); A. Chatzistamatiou, K. Rülling, Higher
direct images of the structure sheaf in positive characteristic, Algebra & Number Theory 5 (2011)
693-775, sections 2-3; V. Srinivas, Gysin maps and cycle classes for Hodge cohomology, Proc. Indian
Acad. Sci. Math. Sci. 103 (1993) 209-247; Hartshorne, Residues and Duality (1966) III.9 for the
symbol.

See also `Lib.Cohomology.WoodsHole` and `Lib.Cohomology.PointClass.LinearIndependence`.

modules.title: Projective Noether normalisation and homogeneous coordinates of embedded points
modules.group: Hodge–Tate images of classes of points
modules.note:
Let k be a field. For a tuple `g : ι → L`, `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsHomogeneousSolution k g w`
says that every homogeneous polynomial over k that vanishes at g also vanishes at w. The file proves
projective Noether normalisation by linear forms in characteristic zero and constructs its Galois
closure.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsNoetherNormalization Λ g`: the linear forms `Λ₀, …, Λ_d` are a Noether
  normalisation of the cone, that is, their values at `g` are independent and the cone is integral
  over them.
* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.exists_isNoetherNormalization`: such forms exist for a non-zero finite
  tuple `g` over a field `k` of characteristic zero.
* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsNoetherNormalization.GaloisClosure`,
  `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsNoetherNormalization.nonempty_galoisClosure`: the Galois closure of
  the normalisation, a finite algebra `B` over `k[X₀, …, X_d]` with points `b σ` of the cone,
  indexed by a finite group.
* `New.Variety.IsCoordsWithUnit.exists_universal_chart`,
  `New.Variety.IsCoordsWithUnit.exists_mem_open_of_isUnit`: a point ξ over a field F with
  coordinates g spreads out and specialises to the vectors w with w i (resp. aeval w b) a unit that
  satisfy the homogeneous relations of g.
* `New.Variety.IsCoordsWithUnit.exists_app_eq_algebraMap_of_isHomogeneousSolution`: over an
  algebraically closed k, a global function takes one constant value on all such specialisations.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LineBundle.IsHomogeneousCoords`: v is a vector of homogeneous coordinates of the point t for
  L: t lands in U_j exactly when v_j is a unit, and then g_jk(t) = v_k/v_j.
* `New.Variety.IsOpenSubfunctor`: V is an open subfunctor of X: each x ∈ X(A) has an ideal I of A
  such that, for φ: A → B, φ(x) ∈ V(B) iff φ(I)B = B.

modules.title: Projective space as a functor, and injective pull-back along Noether normalisation
modules.group: Hodge–Tate images of classes of points
modules.note:
Projective space `ℙ^d` over a field `k` is defined as a functor on `k`-algebras. It is the test
variety on which the Hodge–Tate map is shown not to kill the class of a point.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.projSpace`: `A ↦` unimodular vectors in `A ^ (d + 1)` modulo units of `A`.
* `New.Variety.projSpace.stdChart`, `New.Variety.projSpace.hasAtlas`: the `d + 1` standard charts
  form an atlas.
* `New.Variety.projSpace.lineProductMap`: a map `ℙ^d × ℙ¹ → ℙ^(d+1)`, used for induction on the
  dimension; `New.Variety.projSpace.isUnit_mul_sum_of_mul_eq_zero` and
  `New.Variety.projSpace.exists_eq_map_affinePoint_of_mul_eq_zero` describe the points where all
  its coordinates but the first vanish.
* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsNoetherNormalization.pullback_injective`: pull-back along the
  projection to `ℙ^d` of a subfunctor of `Y × ℙ^d` that contains the graph of a Noether
  normalisation is injective on cohomology of `p`-adic tests.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.unimodular`: the subfunctor of affine `d`-space of vectors whose entries generate
  the unit ideal.
* `New.Variety.IsCoordsWithUnit L x v`: `v` is a vector of homogeneous coordinates, for the line
  bundle `L`, of the point `x` of `Y`, and some entry of `v` is a unit.
* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsHomogeneousSolution k g v`: every homogeneous polynomial over `k` that
  vanishes at `g` vanishes at `v`.
* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsNoetherNormalization Λ g`: the values at `g` of the linear forms
  `Λ 0, …, Λ d` satisfy no non-zero homogeneous relation, and the cone of `g` is integral over them.
* `New.Variety.IsTest`: a test ring: reduced, absolutely integrally closed, and any `a`, `b`
  admit an idempotent `e` with `a ∣ e * b` and `b ∣ (1 - e) * a`.

modules.title: The Hodge–Tate map does not kill point classes of the projective line and space
modules.group: Hodge–Tate images of classes of points
modules.note:
Let `k` be a field with an embedding in `ℚ̄_p`, and let `λ_h = New.Variety.hodgeTateMap h` be the
Hodge–Tate map of weight `h`, from Hodge cohomology to `p`-adic cohomology. We compute `λ₁` of the
symbol `[dT / T]` of the pair `(𝔸¹, 𝔸¹ ∖ 0)` through the extension `0 → T → Bˣ → Tˣ → 0`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.thickeningOver.oneSubMu`, `New.Variety.thickeningOver.shortExact_oneSubMu`: the short
  exact sequence `0 → T → Bˣ → Tˣ → 0` whose first map is `t ↦ 1 - μ t`.
* `New.Variety.hodgeTateMap_symbolClass`: the image of `[dT / T]` comes from the product of the
  boundary class of the pair with the class of this extension.
* `New.Variety.projSpace.exists_hodgeTateMap_pointClass_line`: `λ₁` of the class of `[1 : 0]` in
  `ℙ¹` comes from a degree-two class `η` on `p`-adic tests such that `x ↦ x × η` is injective on
  functors with flat values.
* `New.Variety.projSpace.hodgeTateMap_pointClass_ne_zero`: the class of a point of `ℙ^d` has a
  nonzero image under the Hodge–Tate map of weight `d`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.PadicTest`: a `p`-adic test, a non-empty family of cells (`New.Variety.IsCell`) with
  a ring map from `O_C` to their product; `R` denotes its ring.
* `New.Variety.thickeningOver`: the functor sending a `p`-adic test with ring `R` to the `k`-algebra
  `B = W(R♭)[1/p] / (ker θ)²`. `New.Variety.genericOver` sends it to `T = R[1/p]`, and
  `New.Variety.thickeningOver.proj : B → T` is the projection; its kernel is `μ T`, `μ = [ε] - 1`.
* `New.Variety.hodgeTateMap`: `λ_h` sends a Hodge class to a class on Hodge–Tate pairs (a `p`-adic
  test with a finite free module `M` over `T`). It restricts along `B ×_T (T ⊕ M) → T ⊕ M`, applies
  the `h`-th power of the contraction class, and projects `⋀M` to degree zero.
  `New.Variety.restrictToPairs` maps cohomology on `p`-adic tests to the same target.
* `New.Variety.symbolClass`: the class `[dT / T]` in the Hodge cohomology of the pair
  `(𝔸^d, 𝔸^d ∖ 0)`.
* `New.Variety.pointClass`: the class of a `k`-point `z` in Hodge cohomology of degree `d`, the
  image of a chosen class with support `z` and multiplicity `1` at `z`. Projective space
  `New.Variety.projSpace k d` sends `A` to the unimodular vectors in `A ^ (d + 1)` modulo units.

modules.title: The Hodge–Tate map keeps classes of points on a projective variety linearly independent
modules.group: Hodge–Tate images of classes of points
modules.note:
Let `k` be an algebraically closed field with a map to `Q̄_p`, and let `Y` be a projectively
embedded scheme whose points over `k`-algebras (`New.Variety.algPointsOf`; `PointsIn Y A` is the set
of points of `Y` with values in a `k`-algebra `A`, and `structureMap` is the map `k ⟶ A`) are
covered by charts with `d` étale coordinates (`New.Variety.HasAtlas`). The Hodge–Tate map
`New.Variety.hodgeTateMap d` sends the distinct classes of `k`-points of `Y` to linearly independent
elements.

* `New.Variety.linearIndepOn_hodgeTateMap_pointClass`: the main result.
* `New.Variety.exists_map_separating_class`: for a `k`-point `z₀` and finitely many other points, a
  map `j` to `Y` whose pull-back kills the classes that differ from that of `z₀` and keeps the
  Hodge–Tate image of the class of `z₀` non-zero.

The map `j` is an open part of the graph of a linear projection of the component of `z₀` to
projective space, chosen by Noether normalisation (`New.Variety.exists_generic_chart`,
`New.Variety.exists_etale_projection`). Over a suitable `k`-point `Q` of projective space the
projection is étale and its fibre consists of points with the class of `z₀`. Pull-back along the
projection is injective and the Hodge–Tate image of the class of `Q` is non-zero, so the Hodge–Tate
image of the class of `z₀` is non-zero too.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.pointClass d z`: the class of the `k`-point `z` in the Hodge cohomology of degree
  `d`.
* `New.Variety.IsCoordsWithUnit L x v`: `v` is a vector of homogeneous coordinates of the point `x`
  for the embedding `L`, and some entry of `v` is a unit.
* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsHomogeneousSolution k g v`: every homogeneous polynomial over `k` that
  vanishes at `g` vanishes at `v`, that is, `v` lies on the cone cut out at `g`.
* `New.Variety.CutsOutLocus.IsNoetherNormalization Λ g`: the values `evalForms Λ g` of the linear
  forms `Λ j` satisfy no non-zero homogeneous relation, and the cone of `g` is integral over them.
* `New.Variety.EtaleChart d X`: a `k`-algebra `c.coordRing` with `d` étale coordinates and a point
  `c.point` of `X` with values in `c.coordRing`, whose images `c.locus` (the points
  `X.map φ c.point`) make its spectrum an open subfunctor of `X`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Hodge–Tate images of point classes are non-zero and detect degrees of zero-cycles.
This file proves only that the Hodge–Tate images of the distinct point classes are linearly
independent, without duality or a trace map. Non-vanishing on projective space is imported
(`New.Variety.projSpace.hodgeTateMap_pointClass_ne_zero`) and carried to a smooth projective variety
by transfer along a finite linear projection. Source: Faltings, p-adic Hodge theory, JAMS 1 (1988)
(compatibility with traces and cycle classes); for transfer, Suslin–Voevodsky, Singular homology of
abstract algebraic varieties, Invent. Math. 123 (1996), §§4–6.

modules.title: Tate module, Kummer sequence and the first Chern class of O(1) on the projective line
modules.group: The projective line formula and Chern class of O(1)
modules.note:
Let `g` be a functor from `C` to tests over a ring `A`, and let `ℓ` be a prime. The Tate module `𝕋`
of `G_m` along `g` sits in the Kummer sequence. When `A` is local and absolutely integrally closed
and `ℓ` is invertible in `A`, a section `ε` of `𝕋` makes `𝕋` act on every coefficient `M`
(`New.Variety.TorsionCoeff`: killed by `ℓ`, with Zariski descent). On the projective line `ℙ¹`, the
cocycle of `O(1)` and the Kummer class give the first Chern class `η ∈ H²(ℙ¹, 𝕋)`, and the
projective line formula `H(ℙ¹ × S) = H(S) ⊕ η H(S)` is stated as a property of a coefficient.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.shortExact_kummerSeq`: the Kummer sequence 0 → 𝕋 → Hom(ℚ, G_m) → G_m → 0 is exact.
* `New.Variety.tateGen`, `New.Variety.isCohomEquiv_tensorPoint_tateGen`: a section ε of 𝕋 such that
  S → S ⊗ 𝕋, x ↦ x ⊗ ε, is bijective on Ext(−, F) for S killed by ℓ and F with Zariski descent. Here
  A is local and absolutely integrally closed, and the prime ℓ is invertible in A
  (`New.Variety.InvertsPrime`).
* `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.tateAction`: the class in Ext⁰(M ⊗ 𝕋, M) inverse to x ↦ x ⊗ ε; it
  commutes with all classes between coefficients (`New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.tateAction_comm`).
* `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.mulClass`: the product y · ξ of a class y in M with a class ξ in 𝕋,
  natural in M.
* `New.Variety.etaClass`: the class `η ∈ H²(ℙ¹, 𝕋)`, the cocycle class times the Kummer class.
* `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.etaAt`, `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.HasLineFormula`: product with `η`;
  `H(ℙ¹ × S) = H(S) ⊕ η H(S)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsTest`: a test ring A is reduced and absolutely integrally closed, and any a, b ∈ A
  admit an idempotent e with a ∣ eb and b ∣ (1 − e)a.
* `New.Variety.TestOver`: The category of tests over A: the full subcategory of commutative
  A-algebras whose underlying rings are test rings.
* `New.Variety.H`: The group Ext^n(N,F) in the category of functors from C to abelian groups.
* `New.Variety.Cocycle`: A 1-cocycle from F to G: homomorphisms D(f): F(c) → G(d) for f: c → d with
  D(gf) = G(g)D(f) + D(g)F(f). It defines an extension of F by G.

modules.title: The perfect projective line glued from two perfect discs has the cohomology of a point
modules.group: The projective line formula and Chern class of O(1)
modules.note:
The perfect projective line on p-adic tests S is a model on which classes on ℙ¹ are computed. Its
two discs are represented in the tilt S^♭ by O^♭[ℚ≥0], and its torus by O^♭[ℚ].

* `New.Variety.PerfectLine.gluing`: the gluing map ℤ[torus ⊔ point] → ℤ[two discs]; it is injective
  (a monomorphism). Its cokernel plays the role of the perfect line with the point ∞ killed.
* `New.Variety.PerfectLine.oneSub_comp_gluing`: the operators 1 − (T^s ↦ χ(s) T^s) commute with the
  gluing map.
* `New.Variety.PerfectLine.isCohomEquiv_gluing_tilt`,
  `New.Variety.PerfectLine.isCohomEquiv_gluing_generic`: over each test c the gluing map induces
  bijections on cohomology. This holds for coefficients G(S^♭), where G is built from an O^♭-module
  N and is assumed acyclic on perfect rings. It also holds for S[1/p].
* `New.Variety.PerfectLine.subsingleton_H_cokernel_gluing`: then M ⊗ cokernel has no cohomology, for
  every M with flat values.

Idea: all cohomology is in degree 0, where the map is the splitting of a Laurent polynomial into two
parts according to the sign of the exponent. `New.Period.OFlat` is O^♭, the tilt of the ring of
integers O_C of ℂ_p.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.PadicTest`: A p-adic test: a non-empty family of cells (`New.Variety.IsCell`) with a
  ring map from O_C to their product.
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to Z[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A). ℤ[Y] has flat base change (`HasFlatBaseChange`) when tensoring by a
  flat module M commutes with its cohomology with module coefficients.

modules.title: Leray–Hirsch bases and the projective line formula for the tilted theory
modules.group: The projective line formula and Chern class of O(1)
modules.note:
The first part works over the tests `New.Variety.TestOver A` with coefficients killed by `ℓ`. Here
`A` is an absolutely integrally closed local domain in which the prime `ℓ` is invertible (the
instance `New.Variety.InvertsPrime A ℓ`). The projective line formula
(`New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.HasLineFormula`) says that the classes 1 and η identify Ext(S,
F) ⊕ Ext(S, F) with Ext(S, F) taken over the category of points of ℙ¹; here η is
`New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.cupClass`, the product with `New.Variety.etaClass` at the tautological
point of ℙ¹.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.isLerayHirschBasis_of_forall_isField`: bijectivity passes from the fields under a
  test to the test, given `New.Variety.IsDetectedAtPoints` (zero sets of classes are open;
  invariance under field extension).
* `New.Variety.exists_isLerayHirschBasis_of_isCohomDense`: a basis exists on the special fibre
  `New.Variety.IdealFamily.ofMaximalIdeal`.
* `New.Variety.isDetectedAtPoints_projLine`: the locally constant `ℤ/ℓ`-valued functions on pairs
  (test over `A`, point of ℙ¹) satisfy `New.Variety.IsDetectedAtPoints`.
* `New.Variety.exists_isTodaCancellation`: from a square `δ' ≫ i = i ≫ δ` with `i` a monomorphism,
  the product η of the classes of two short exact sequences is cancelled
  (`New.Variety.IsTodaCancellation`): after an exact functor that makes the cokernel of `i` acyclic,
  the product with a class ω is onto, and the pull-back of η m along `j` determines the pull-back of
  m along `ε`.
* `New.Variety.isLerayHirschBasis_lineBasis_of_injective`: two conditions on the product with η that
  give the formula at S.
* `New.Variety.hasLineFormula_tiltTheory`: the formula, from the cover of the perfect ℙ¹ by two
  discs.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.TestOver`: The category of tests over A: the full subcategory of commutative
  A-algebras whose underlying rings are test rings.
* `New.Variety.lerayHirsch`: For classes θ_i in Ext^{d_i}(ΦG, F), the Leray–Hirsch map w ↦ Σ
  θ_i∘Φ(w_i) from finitely supported families in total Ext(S, G) to total Ext(ΦS, F);
  `New.Variety.IsLerayHirschBasis` says that it is bijective.
* `New.Variety.H`: The group Ext^n(N,F) in the category of functors from C to abelian groups.
* `New.Variety.projLine`: The projective line as a functor on rings: B goes to the set of points
  (1 + uv : v) with u, v in B, that is, pairs (u, v) modulo `New.Variety.projLineSetoid`.
* `New.Variety.freeAb`: The functor sending a set-valued functor Y to ℤ[Y], whose value at A is the
  free abelian group on Y(A).
modules.literature:
Known result: Künneth formula over a field for mod-ℓ étale cohomology, in Leray–Hirsch form. It is
proved here only over the special fibre of an absolutely integrally closed local domain. It states
that a basis of the cohomology over the residue field that contains a given non-zero class stays a
basis over every test ring of the special fibre. Source: SGA 4 XVII 5.4.3; Milne, Étale Cohomology
VI.8.

See also `Lib.Cohomology.ProjectiveLine.ConstantLineFormula`.

modules.title: The projective line formula for locally constant ℤ/ℓ coefficients
modules.group: The projective line formula and Chern class of O(1)
modules.note:
The projective line formula H(ℙ¹ × S) = H(S) ⊕ η H(S) (`New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.HasLineFormula`) is
proved for the theory `New.Variety.Theory.locallyConstant` of locally constant ℤ/ℓ-valued functions
on tests over an absolutely integrally closed valuation ring A, with ℓ invertible, that embeds into
ℂ_ℓ. Here H is total Ext of functors to abelian groups, η is the degree two class
`New.Variety.TorsionCoeff.cupClass`, and `New.Variety.lerayHirsch θ S` is the Leray–Hirsch map w ↦ Σ
θ_i · w_i of a family θ of classes; θ is a Leray–Hirsch basis at S
(`New.Variety.IsLerayHirschBasis`) when this map is bijective.

* `New.Variety.isLerayHirschBasis_lineBasis_of_basis`: the formula over a flat S follows from any
  family θ that contains η and is a Leray–Hirsch basis over S and over S ⊗ ℤ[ℙ¹].
* `New.Variety.hasLineFormula_of_lerayHirsch_ne_zero`: over a valuation ring A the formula holds as
  soon as η acts non-trivially on the point for one coefficient whose tests lie over the generic
  point of A.
* `New.Variety.hasLineFormula_locallyConstant`: the formula for a valuation ring A with an injective
  ring map to ℂ_ℓ.

The formula is reduced to algebraically closed fields k over A
(`New.Variety.hasUniversalPoints_structurePt`), where a Künneth basis contains η unless η · 1 = 0.
That vanishing would spread to the generic point of A; the tilted theory of
`New.Variety.hasLineFormula_tiltTheory` shows that it does not occur for A in ℂ_ℓ.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.TestOver`: The category of tests over A: the commutative A-algebras that are reduced,
  absolutely integrally closed, and in which any a, b admit an idempotent e with a ∣ eb and
  b ∣ (1 − e)a.
* `New.Variety.TorsionCoeff`: A coefficient along g: a functor to abelian groups, killed by ℓ, with
  Zariski descent; a `New.Variety.Theory` is one that also behaves well on closed loci.
* `New.Variety.projLine`: The projective line as a functor on rings; `New.Variety.onePointFunctor`
  is the constant one-point functor and `New.Variety.reprBy A` the functor Hom(A, −).
modules.literature:
Known result: the projective line formula for ℤ/ℓ coefficients, where the degree two class is the
Chern class of O(1) given by the Kummer sequence. Here the formula H(ℙ¹ × S) = H(S) ⊕ η H(S) is
stated in Leray–Hirsch form for locally constant ℤ/ℓ coefficients on test rings; the tilted
coefficients serve only to show that η acts non-trivially. Source: SGA 4½ [Cycle]; SGA 5
(Jouanolou); Milne, Étale Cohomology; Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties.

modules.title: Mayer–Vietoris for two charts of a line modulo an ideal
modules.group: Proper base change for ℤ/ℓ-cohomology on test rings
modules.note:
This file gives the commutative algebra behind a Mayer–Vietoris sequence of locally constant
`ZMod ℓ`-valued functions for two charts of a line. The setting is two charts `Spec B`, `Spec C`
over `A` with overlap `Spec D`, where `D = B[1 / t] = C[1 / s]`, `t * s = 1` in `D`, and `D` is
integral over `A[t, s]`. Everything is read modulo an ideal `I` of `A`. Under further hypotheses,
compatible clopens of the charts come from the base, and every locally constant function on the
overlap is a difference of functions from the charts.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.exists_eq_basicOpen_of_isClopen_of_preimage_eq`: compatible clopens of the charts
  come from `A`, assuming every pair in `B × C` agreeing in `D` comes from `A` (`hA_onto`) and `hI`.
* `New.Variety.exists_eq_locConstSpec_map_sub_map`: under further hypotheses (`A`, `D` domains; `ℓ`
  prime and a unit in `A`; `A`, `B`, `C` absolutely integrally closed; `hI`; `h_cases`), every
  locally constant `ZMod ℓ`-valued function on the overlap is a difference of functions from the
  charts.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed`: A is absolutely integrally closed: every monic polynomial
  over A of positive degree has a root in A.
* `New.ThePrime`: `ThePrime ℓ` fixes the prime `ℓ` (it extends `Fact ℓ.Prime`).
* `New.Variety.locConstSpec`: For an abelian group Λ, the functor on commutative rings sending A to
  the group of locally constant functions Spec A → Λ; it sends a ring map to pull-back along the map
  of spectra.

modules.title: The space of places of residue fields and its properness over the base
modules.group: Proper base change for ℤ/ℓ-cohomology on test rings
modules.note:
Spaces are functors from rings to sets (`New.Variety.PointFunctor`). For `s : Z ⟶ reprBy D` and a
point `x ∈ Z(C)`, the ring map under `x` is `baseRingMap s x : D ⟶ C`. The space of places is a form
of the Riemann–Zariski space. It is used to cover a proper functor `Z` over `D`.

A place of a `D`-algebra `P` is a prime `q` of `P` together with a valuation ring of `κ(q)` over
`D`. For `α : D ⟶ P`, the ring `T = prodValuationRing α` is the product of these valuation rings.
Each `t ∈ P` is a ratio `a t / b t` in it, with `a = numerator` and `b = denominator`. The space of
places `W` of a valuative lift `z`, with `z.point ∈ Z(T)`, has as points over `C` the classes of
maps `f : T → C`. Two maps are identified if they give the same point `Z.map f z.point` of `Z(C)`
and the same ratios `(f (a t) : f (b t))`.

* `New.Variety.IsProperOver`: properness, as a closed diagonal and a valuative criterion.
* `New.Variety.ResiduePlace.placeSpace`: the space of places `W`.
* `New.Variety.ResiduePlace.exists_isLocalHom_eq_projHom_comp`: a point of `W` in a local ring comes
  from one place.
* `New.Variety.ResiduePlace.isProperOver_placeSpace`: the space of places is proper over `D`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.reprBy D`: the functor `Hom(D, −)` represented by `D`.

modules.title: Splitting absolutely integrally closed subrings with a Mayer–Vietoris sequence
modules.group: Proper base change for ℤ/ℓ-cohomology on test rings
modules.note:
This file gives a splitting step in an induction over the absolutely integrally closed subrings of
an algebraically closed field `K` that contain the image of `γ : D →+* K`. A subring `B` of this
kind that is not a valuation ring is replaced by the integral closures of `B[t]` and `B[1 / t]`,
as in the cover of a projective line by two charts. These two larger rings fit into a short exact
Mayer–Vietoris sequence of locally constant `ZMod ℓ`-valued functions on the spectra modulo `J`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.absIntegrallyClosedSubrings`: the absolutely integrally closed subrings of `K`
  containing the image of `γ`.
* `New.Variety.absIntegrallyClosedSubrings.quotientFunctor`: the functor `B ↦ B / J B` on these
  subrings.
* `New.Variety.absIntegrallyClosedSubrings.exists_isSplitting_isMayerVietorisExact`: the two larger
  rings and a short exact Mayer–Vietoris sequence of locally constant `ZMod ℓ`-valued functions on
  the spectra modulo `J`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed`: A is absolutely integrally closed: every monic polynomial
  over A of positive degree has a root in A.
* `New.ThePrime`: `ThePrime ℓ` fixes the prime `ℓ` (it extends `Fact ℓ.Prime`).
* `New.Variety.locConstSpec`: For an abelian group Λ, the functor on commutative rings sending A to
  the group of locally constant functions Spec A → Λ; it sends a ring map to pull-back along the map
  of spectra.
* `New.Variety.IsLineChartCase` (in `Lib.Cohomology.ProperBaseChange.LineCharts`): the condition on
  the chart `R[1 / a]` of a line modulo an ideal `I` of `R`.

modules.title: Proper base change over AIC valuation rings and its consequences for ℤ/ℓ-cohomology
modules.group: Proper base change for ℤ/ℓ-cohomology on test rings
modules.note:
Spaces are functors on rings. A space is proper over `A` (`New.Variety.IsProperOver`) if its
diagonal is cut out by ideals and a valuative criterion holds with one universal point.
`New.Variety.TestOver` A is the category of A-algebras that are test rings (absolutely integrally
closed reduced rings where any two elements are comparable for divisibility after splitting by an
idempotent; `testIncl` includes them in rings), `New.Variety.H` N F n is Extⁿ(N, F) among functors
to abelian groups, and the coefficients are ℤ/ℓ for a prime ℓ invertible in the base. The file
proves proper base change over an absolutely integrally closed local domain that is a valuation ring
and derives three consequences: injectivity of restriction to the residue fibre, invariance of
cohomology under extension of algebraically closed fields, and openness of zero sets of classes.
These results then give detection at points for coefficients that are ℤ/ℓ on the zero locus of a
family of ideals, in the form used to prove that Leray–Hirsch maps are bijective.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Variety.IsProperOver.proper_base_change`: for `Y` proper over an absolutely integrally closed
  valuation ring `A` in which `ℓ` is invertible, the closed fibre of `Y` has the cohomology of `Y`.
* `New.Variety.IsProperOver.injective_map_residue`: over an absolutely integrally closed local
  domain that is a valuation ring, a class is determined by its restriction to the fibre over the
  residue field.
* `New.Variety.IsProperOver.isTestCohomEquiv_field_extension`: cohomology does not change under an
  extension `S → T` of algebraically closed fields over `R`.
* `New.Variety.IsProperOver.isOpen_zero_set_and_eq_zero`: over a test ring, the primes at which a
  class vanishes form an open set, and a class that vanishes at every prime is zero.
* `New.Variety.IsDetectedAtPoints`: the property of a coefficient F that classes over a test are
  detected at the residue fields of its primes (zero sets are open, and a class that vanishes at
  every prime is zero), and that extending a field test changes nothing; a structure with one field
  for each of these two properties.
* `New.Variety.IdealFamily.isDetectedAtPoints_of_proper`: for X proper over ℤ and I a family of
  ideals on X × Spec A, a coefficient that is ℤ/ℓ on the locus I = 0, this locus being dense, has
  that property. Idea: the locus W = {I = 0} is proper over A, and over a test c the cohomology with
  coefficients F is that of W_c with coefficients ℤ/ℓ.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosedLocal`: A is an absolutely integrally closed local domain: a
  local domain in which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomEquiv`: α : N' → N induces bijections Extⁿ(N, F) → Extⁿ(N', F) for all n.
* `New.Variety.locConstCoeff` Λ: the coefficient on test rings given by the locally constant
  functions Spec B → Λ.
* `New.Variety.IsTestCohomEquiv` Λ u: the map u of functors on rings, restricted to test rings,
  induces such bijections for the coefficient `locConstCoeff Λ`.
* `New.Variety.reprBy`: the functor h_A = Hom(A, −) represented by A.
* `New.Variety.IsCohomDense`: U ⊆ Y is dense for F if for every point h_A → Y the inclusion of the
  preimage of U in h_A is such an equivalence.
* `New.Variety.IdealFamily`: For a functor ι from C to commutative rings, ideals I_c of ι(c) such
  that I_b is generated by the image of I_a for every morphism a → b.
* `New.Variety.zeroPoints`: For s: X → h_R and a subset I of R, the subfunctor of points x ∈ X(B)
  whose structure map R → B sends I to 0; `New.Variety.unitPoints`: those whose structure map sends
  every element of I to a unit.

Known result: Proper base change and invariance under extension of algebraically closed fields. Here
the coefficients are constant F_ℓ, the base is an absolutely integrally closed valuation ring, and
properness of a functor (`New.Variety.IsProperOver`) means a closed diagonal and a valuative
criterion. The proof reduces to spaces of places of a field and then uses Zorn's lemma on subrings
with a Mayer–Vietoris splitting, together with Kummer theory. Source: Artin, SGA 4 Exp. XII 5.1,
5.4, 5.5 (1973); Stacks Project Tag 095S; reduction to spaces of places as in Scholze, Étale
cohomology of diamonds (2017), Thm 19.2 and Lemma 19.4, after Huber, Math. Ann. 295 (1993).
